summary: Coenzyme Q10 (ubiquinone, ubidecarenone) is a naturally occurring, fat-soluble compound essential to mitochondrial electron transport and ATP production, and a lipid antioxidant. It is marketed as a dietary supplement and used for statin-associated muscle symptoms, heart failure, mitochondrial disorders, migraine prophylaxis and general antioxidant support. It is NOT an FDA-approved drug; doses and uses below reflect supplement/EMA/reference information rather than an approved label.

Statin-associated muscle symptoms (commonly used, mixed evidence)
Primary and secondary coenzyme Q10 deficiency / mitochondrial disorders

dosage.n: Take with dietary fat for absorption
As adjunct to standard therapy, not a substitute

Around 100 mg three times daily (~300 mg/day)
dosage.n: Effect develops over weeks to months

moa: Coenzyme Q10 is an essential component of the mitochondrial electron transport chain, shuttling electrons between complexes I/II and complex III to drive oxidative phosphorylation and ATP generation. In its reduced form (ubiquinol) it is a potent lipid-phase antioxidant that protects cell membranes and lipoproteins from oxidative damage and helps regenerate other antioxidants such as vitamin E. Supplementation aims to restore reduced endogenous levels (e.g., with aging, statin therapy, heart failure, or genetic deficiency).

absolute: Known hypersensitivity to a coenzyme Q10 product or its excipients
relative: Concurrent warfarin therapy (possible reduced anticoagulant effect)
Uncontrolled hypotension (may modestly lower blood pressure)
monitor: Blood pressure in patients on antihypertensives
Glycemic control in diabetes (possible minor effects)

preg: There is insufficient safety data in pregnancy. Use only on the advice of a clinician when potential benefit justifies the unknown risk.
lact: There is insufficient data on use during breastfeeding. Use only on the advice of a clinician.
renal: No specific dose adjustment is established; coenzyme Q10 has limited renal handling. Use with general caution.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is established. Use with general caution.

moderate: Warfarin - may reduce anticoagulant effect (structural similarity to vitamin K); monitor INR
Antihypertensives - may have additive blood-pressure-lowering effect
minor: Statins - lower endogenous CoQ10 levels (rationale for supplementation)
Insulin / oral hypoglycemics - possible minor effect on glucose; monitor
Chemotherapy agents - theoretical antioxidant interaction; discuss with oncologist
interactions.food: Take with a fat-containing meal to maximize absorption of this lipophilic compound.

serious: Generally none at usual doses; well tolerated
emergency: Severe allergic reaction (rare) with swelling or breathing difficulty

counsel: This is a dietary supplement, not a substitute for prescribed medicines
Take it with a meal that contains some fat so your body absorbs it better
Tell your doctor you are taking it, especially if you are on a blood thinner (warfarin) or blood-pressure medicines
Benefits for conditions like migraine can take several weeks to appear
Stop and seek advice if you develop a rash or any allergic symptoms
pk: Plasma levels rise over hours; clinical effects over weeks in chronic conditions
Peak plasma concentration about 6 hours after an oral dose (delayed, lipophilic)
Long half-life supports once- to thrice-daily dosing
Store at room temperature, protected from light and moisture
pearls: NOT an FDA-approved drug - it is a dietary supplement; doses/uses reflect supplement and reference sources, and product quality varies
Highly lipophilic - absorption is markedly improved when taken with dietary fat
May reduce the effect of warfarin (vitamin K-like structure) - monitor INR
Statins lower endogenous CoQ10 - a common rationale for use in statin-associated muscle symptoms (evidence is mixed)
Generally very well tolerated, with only mild GI effects at usual doses
missed: If a dose is missed, take it when remembered with food. If it is nearly time for the next dose, skip the missed one - do not double up. As a supplement, occasional missed doses are not harmful.
overdose: Coenzyme Q10 has a wide safety margin and overdose is not associated with serious toxicity; excess intake may cause gastrointestinal upset. Manage symptomatically and discontinue if needed.
